summary.short: Amends Sections 10 and 20 of Illinois's Biometric Information Privacy Act: sets definitions for biometric identifiers and information and a right of action with liquidated damages against private entities. Takes effect upon becoming law.
summary.long: Public Act 103-0769 amends Sections 10 and 20 of the Biometric Information Privacy Act (740 ILCS 14). Section 10 defines biometric identifiers (retina or iris scan, fingerprint, voiceprint, or scan of hand or face geometry) and biometric information, and lists exclusions such as photographs, writing samples, donated organs and medical imaging. It also defines confidential and sensitive information, electronic signature, private entity (excluding State or local government agencies and Illinois courts) and written release. Section 20 gives any aggrieved person a right of action in a State circuit court or as a supplemental claim in federal district court against an offending party. A prevailing party may recover liquidated damages of $1,000 for a negligent violation by a private entity or $5,000 for an intentional or reckless one, or actual damages if greater, plus attorneys' fees, costs and other relief such as an injunction. Repeated instances of collecting or disclosing the same biometric data from the same person, by the same method and to the same recipient, count as a single violation of Section 15(b) or 15(d), which is not reproduced in this Act. The Act takes effect upon becoming law.

notes: Excerpt of enrolled bill text with page headers and broken line breaks interleaved; the enrolled text does not mark inserted or deleted words, so the changes made to Sections 10 and 20 cannot be identified from this document. Section 5 amends only Sections 10 and 20 of the Biometric Information Privacy Act. Section 99 sets the effective date as upon becoming law, with no calendar date. Sec. 20(b) and (c) refer to subsections of Section 15 of the Act, which is not in this text. The Act's addressee is the defined class 'private entity' (Sec. 10), which is not a named entity.

evidence.quote: amended by changing Sections 10 and 20 as follows:
"Biometric identifier" means a retina or iris scan, fingerprint, voiceprint, or scan of hand or face geometry.
"Biometric information" means any information, regardless of how it is captured, converted, stored, or shared, based on an individual's biometric identifier used to identify an individual.
"Confidential and sensitive information" means personal information that can be used to uniquely identify an individual or an individual's account or property.
"Electronic signature" means an electronic sound, symbol, or process attached to or logically associated with a record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record.
State or local government agency. A private entity does not
"Written release" means informed written consent, electronic signature, or, in the context of employment, a release executed by an employee as a condition of employment.

enforcement.authority: State circuit court or federal district court (private action by an aggrieved person against an offending party)
enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of a provision of the Biometric Information Privacy Act by a private entity; any person aggrieved by the violation may sue
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Liquidated damages of $1,000 per negligent violation or $5,000 per intentional or reckless violation, or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus attorneys' fees and costs and other relief including an injunction
enforcement.penalty_formula: Per violation: $1,000 for a negligent violation (Sec. 20(a)(1)); $5,000 for an intentional or reckless violation (Sec. 20(a)(2)); each at liquidated damages or actual damages, whichever is greater. Attorneys' fees and costs, expert witness fees and other relief including an injunction are also recoverable (Sec. 20(a)(3)-(4)). Under Sec. 20(b) and (c), repeated instances of the same collection, or of the same disclosure to the same recipient by the same method, count as a single violation with at most one recovery.

evidence.quote: liquidated damages of $1,000 or actual damages, whichever is greater

entities.note: No named firms, facilities or public bodies. The Act addresses the defined class 'private entity' (Sec. 10), which excludes State or local government agencies and Illinois courts.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment. The dollar amounts in Sec. 20(a)(1)-(2) are damages, coded as enforcement. The 'more than one instance' language in Sec. 20(b)-(c) is not numeric.

obligations.note: The document amends only the definitions in BIPA Sec. 10 and the right-of-action provisions in Sec. 20. Both are definitions, scope exclusions or enforcement and recovery rules, which the codebook excludes from obligations. The consent and notice duties of private entities sit in BIPA Sec. 15, which this act does not amend or reproduce. Changed text is not marked in the document, so no new operative duty could be identified.
